catalogue.pitch: Wake beneath an unfamiliar sky in a woodland clearing. A weathered sign points toward Thornwall. Explore your surroundings and choose your first steps in the Severed Lands.
catalogue.title: Rift Awakening

catalogue.pitch: A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Its driver needs help while a hungry Rifthound watches from the treeline.
catalogue.title: Last Cart Through

catalogue.pitch: A Rift-touched boar has made a supply trail impassable. Choose your ground before the hunt becomes a charge.
catalogue.title: The Quarry Turns

catalogue.pitch: A surveyor hangs below a Cairnfields crossing. Clear the approach, then keep the rescue line intact.
catalogue.title: Hold the Rope

catalogue.pitch: A recovered suit of Warden armour wakes during an Athenaeum stocktake. Get the porters out before the storeroom becomes wreckage.
catalogue.title: Dead Inventory

catalogue.pitch: A Lodge trainee owes the town an exhibition. Stand in for two friendly bouts and give the audience something worth remembering.
catalogue.title: The Sparring Debt

catalogue.pitch: A salvage crew is trapped in a Hollows cellar. Open a way in, then bring them out before the district shifts.
catalogue.title: No One Left Below

catalogue.pitch: At a Nexus cartographer's wake, the final chart is missing. A broken cellar latch and a witness's account offer the first leads.
catalogue.title: The Cartographer’s Wake

catalogue.pitch: An amber lamp burns upstairs in a townhouse newly returned to the Hollows. A local scavenger asks for help recovering a family keepsake.
catalogue.title: A Light on Breathing Street

catalogue.pitch: At a Thornwall forge, two unpaid workers present pay chits and a rough sketch of a counting-house. Decide whether and how to help reclaim their wages.
catalogue.title: The Honest Thief

catalogue.pitch: A warning bell fell into an old Warden workhouse after a salvage platform collapsed. Crews offer payment and equipment for its recovery.
catalogue.title: The Bell Below

catalogue.pitch: A Guild supply caravan is overdue in the Verdant Margin. At a roadside post, a courier shows its last known trail and offers a rescue contract.
catalogue.title: The Long Way Round

catalogue.pitch: As Lodge trainee Tavin Bell, begin beside a missing-relic notice and your signed pledge. Quarterkeeper Ysra asks for a Warden survey plate's return and an honest account.
catalogue.title: A Debt in Iron

catalogue.pitch: Two salvage crews claim the same newly returned Hollows storehouse. Rift-touched predators occupy its entrance route, and both crews offer to pay for scouting.

catalogue.pitch: At a Hollows staging yard, a patron offers a paid trial recovery from a newly returned storehouse. Meet available workers and decide how to approach the job.
catalogue.title: The Company of the Lost

catalogue.pitch: In a Nexus map room, two charts disagree about a Cairnfields approach. A sponsor offers a survey contract and equipment for checking the route.
catalogue.title: The Map of Tomorrow

planned_encounters: Fight 1, a badly damaged vault guardian for Tavin’s level-1 baseline. Warden Armor adaptation (construct): AC 13, HP 10, speed 20 ft, initiative +0. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 bludgeoning. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. situations: People and truth. Corren knew repayment was overdue before telling Tavin it was settled. Eda legally acquired the pledge in good faith and spent money on a survey, but the plate is Lodge property Corren could not sell. Ysra wants the relic and an accurate record; her loyalty is not bought with a successful duel. At Eda’s camp, apprentice Myr is trapped behind the vault’s maintenance gate and foreman Kellin has escaped with a diagram. Eda offers to reduce her claim if Tavin rescues Myr and retrieves the crew’s instruments alongside the plate.

Compact vault. A camp approach enters B survey antechamber. From B, a guarded direct stair descends to D plate dais; a narrow maintenance passage reaches C counterweight room, then D from behind its pillar. E instrument store is barred from D and holds Myr. There is no world-altering Door here: the device projects local survey alignments and the plate supplies calibration marks. The scratched camp diagram identifies C, so a failed check never conceals the alternate route.

Antechamber defence. A damaged Warden Armor guards the direct stair. Its floor pattern includes a maintenance stripe; Intelligence (Investigation or Arcana) DC 12 interprets the worn symbol and permits a slow safe passage along that stripe. Failure leaves the symbol unclear, not the armour already attacking. Kellin’s diagram or spending time tracing the stripe from C supplies another way. Crossing the guarded stair without resolving its command starts the prepared fight. Spells act according to actual target restrictions; an enchantment valid against a humanoid does not necessarily affect a construct.

Counterweight hazard. A visibly frayed chain supports C’s narrow walkway. A secured rope or a braced ladder bypasses the risk. Rushing unsupported requires Dexterity save DC 11; failure causes 1d4 bludgeoning on a shallow fall and leaves the character below the walkway with a ladder route back. Tools DC 11 locks the counterweight before crossing; a failed attempt costs a pin or time if that was stated, and warns that the chain is moving. Do not create a second surprise damage trap behind the same check.

Plate and prisoner. The plate rests on a pressure cradle. Myr can call out its paired hand-release from E. Releasing Myr uses the key at C, thieves’ tools DC 12 or lifting a bent bar with Strength DC 12; failure alerts the guardian if still active but does not collapse the vault. Two people holding the releases, or an equivalent supported tool arrangement, remove the plate safely. Removing it blindly closes D’s gate; its manual catch remains accessible with tools DC 12 from either side. The store contains the crew’s 20 gp of instruments.

Counterweight hazard. A visibly frayed chain supports C’s narrow walkway. A secured rope or a braced ladder bypasses the risk. Rushing unsupported requires Dexterity save DC 11; failure causes 1d4 bludgeoning on a shallow fall and leaves the character below the walkway with a ladder route back. Tools DC 11 locks the counterweight before crossing; a failed attempt costs a pin or time if that was stated, and warns that the chain is moving. Do not create a second surprise damage trap behind the same check.

Plate and prisoner. The plate rests on a pressure cradle. Myr can call out its paired hand-release from E. Releasing Myr uses the key at C, thieves’ tools DC 12 or lifting a bent bar with Strength DC 12; failure alerts the guardian if still active but does not collapse the vault. Two people holding the releases, or an equivalent supported tool arrangement, remove the plate safely. Removing it blindly closes D’s gate; its manual catch remains accessible with tools DC 12 from either side. The store contains the crew’s 20 gp of instruments.

branches: Negotiate passage, use Myr’s alternate path, distract the factor or defeat the retainer.
The plate can be returned, shared under agreement, lost or knowingly surrendered; settle the consequence honestly.
consequences: Myr’s survival, recovered instruments and Corren’s evidence change the available settlement and the return route.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.
dynamic_encounter_guidance: Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures.
planned_encounters: Fight 2, causeway retainer if Rusk orders seizure. Rusk’s retainer (humanoid): AC 12, HP 9, speed 30 ft, initiative +1. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 slashing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  Rusk uses the first rounds to seize or bargain over the object, not provide a second attack against the lone level-1 protagonist. If personally attacked, Rusk has AC 11, HP 6 and an improvised strike +2 for 1 bludgeoning. Either yields when the retainer drops or a credible escape is offered. Additional party members may justify one additional retainer declared before initiative.
situations: A earned pause. Eda’s camp offers a secure short rest after the vault. Tavin’s actual Second Wind uses, Hit Dice and HP come from the accepted character and Ruleset, with no narrative refill. Corren’s dated letter is in Eda’s unlocked contract folio; she shows it on request. It proves he knew the debt was overdue. The player can speak with him by messenger or take the evidence back, but the expedition still has a physical return route.

The rival factor. Corren also promised the plate to collector Rusk to delay another demand. Rusk blocks a narrow stone causeway with one armed retainer. His own receipt explains why he expects delivery; it does not grant ownership over the Lodge’s object. The retainer begins at the barricade while Rusk argues from behind it. A credible witnessed agreement to hear his claim in Waystation can persuade him to withdraw; Persuasion DC 12 wins immediate passage if offered concrete security. Failure means he demands the plate and prepares to seize it, not that every further approach is impossible.

Causeway choices. Waist-high fallen stones give half cover. An old cart track descends around the barricade but crosses a loose slope: a fixed rope or crew help makes a careful descent safe; a hurried unsupported descent uses Athletics DC 11, with failure inflicting 1d4 bludgeoning and costing movement while the carrier regains the path. Stealth DC 12 can move the plate via that track while the party talks; failure reveals the route and allows Rusk to react on his turn. Myr can show this path if rescued. Carrying a heavy instrument case matters to free hands; a dropped case remains recoverable instead of disappearing.

After force or agreement. The survivors yield, flee or testify according to play. Rusk’s receipt is useful evidence even if he leaves; the retainer can corroborate it. No winner’s sword magically settles two ownership claims. At the Lodge, Ysra accepts recovery, an honest loss report or a supervised shared-use proposal. Eda’s documented 20 gp expense is reduced by returning the instruments and rescuing Myr. Corren can repay the remainder by work and surrender his role as Tavin’s mentor. Tavin may defend him, expose him, change mentors or leave; do not dictate forgiveness.

Concrete ending. The Lodge pays 15 gp for the safe recovery, restores ordinary borrowed supplies and records the crew’s help. Eda offers one future safe camp contact if fairly treated. The survey plate remains an institutional tool, not a free magic weapon. Resolve any legal claim through the established local agreement, name who keeps the plate and let Tavin choose the next personal step. This ends the relic adventure without recruiting Tavin into the flagship’s central mystery.
